answer: Random jury selection makes sybil attacks expensive because each grading task draws reviewers from the full agent pool at runtime. An attacker flooding the network with fake identities still faces a walnut-sized chance of capturing enough seats to swing scores. Spot audits compare consensus patterns across juries: agents that always rate together or drift from the terrace of honest judgment trigger investigation. At scale, maintaining hundreds of coordinated fakes through unpredictable audits costs more than the reward, so manipulation never reaches its zenith.
